update_log: Complete exhaustive baseline of state-wise major festivals, harvest celebrations, and cultural fairs across India for Static GK.

major_festivals.name: Ugadi
major_festivals.significance: Telugu New Year, celebrated in Chaitra month; preparation of 'Ugadi Pachadi' representing six tastes of life.

major_festivals.name: Tirupati Brahmotsavam
major_festivals.significance: 9-day festival held at Venkateswara Temple in Tirumala, drawing millions of pilgrims.

major_festivals.name: Visakha Utsav
major_festivals.significance: Organized by the state government to promote tourism and local arts in Visakhapatnam.

major_festivals.name: Losar
major_festivals.significance: Tibetan New Year celebrated by the Monpa tribe to usher in prosperity.

major_festivals.name: Solung
major_festivals.significance: Most popular festival of the Adi tribe, spanning seven days, featuring animal sacrifices and rituals for good crops.

major_festivals.name: Mopin
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated by the Galo tribe to drive away evil spirits; involves smearing rice powder (Ette) on faces.

major_festivals.name: Ziro Festival of Music
major_festivals.significance: Outdoor music festival held in the Ziro Valley, showcasing indie artists.

major_festivals.name: Bihu
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated three times a year: Bohag Bihu (Spring New Year), Kati Bihu (Autumn crop protection), and Magh Bihu (Winter harvest feast).

major_festivals.name: Ambubachi Mela
major_festivals.significance: Held annually at Kamakhya Temple, celebrating the earth's fertility during the monsoon.

major_festivals.name: Majuli Festival
major_festivals.significance: Showcases the ethnic culture of the world's largest river island, Majuli.

major_festivals.name: Chhath Puja
major_festivals.significance: Exclusively dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya; involves strict fasting and offering Arghya at riverbanks.

major_festivals.name: Sonepur Cattle Fair
major_festivals.significance: One of Asia's largest cattle fairs, held on Kartik Poornima at the confluence of Gandak and Ganga rivers.

major_festivals.name: Sama Chakeva
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated in the Mithila region, highlighting the sacred bond between brothers and sisters.

major_festivals.name: Bastar Dussehra
major_festivals.significance: World's longest festival, lasting 75 days; dedicated to local deity Danteshwari Mai rather than Rama's victory.

major_festivals.name: Hareli
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated by farmers worshiping farming equipment, cows, and praying for an abundant monsoon crop.

major_festivals.name: Madai Festival
major_festivals.significance: Gond community festival celebrated across Bastar with traditional dances and markets.

major_festivals.name: Shigmo
major_festivals.significance: The Goan counterpart of Holi; features grand street parades, folk dances (Ghodemodni), and colors.

major_festivals.name: Goa Carnival
major_festivals.significance: Introduced by the Portuguese; massive street processions led by King Momo shouting 'Viva Carnaval'.

major_festivals.name: Sao Joao
major_festivals.significance: Feast of St. John the Baptist where local youths wear floral crowns (Kopels) and leap into wells.

major_festivals.name: Navratri
major_festivals.significance: 9 nights of continuous dancing (Garba and Dandiya Raas) honoring Goddess Durga.

major_festivals.name: Uttarayan / International Kite Festival
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated on January 14th; the skies are filled with millions of competitive kites.

major_festivals.name: Modhera Dance Festival
major_festivals.significance: Annual classical dance festival held against the historic backdrop of the Modhera Sun Temple.

major_festivals.name: Surajkund International Crafts Mela
major_festivals.significance: The world's largest crafts fair, showcasing global handloom talent every February in Faridabad.

major_festivals.name: Baisakhi
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated with massive enthusiasm to mark the ripening of the Rabi wheat crop.

major_festivals.name: Kullu Dussehra
major_festivals.significance: Begins when Dussehra ends in the rest of India; over 200 local hill deities assemble at Dhalpur Maidan.

major_festivals.name: Minjar Fair
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated in Chamba; symbolized by throwing silk tassels/minjar (representing maize shoots) into the Ravi river.

major_festivals.name: Fagli Utsav
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated in Kinnaur to mark the end of winter and victory of good over evil.

major_festivals.name: Herath (Maha Shivratri)
major_festivals.significance: The most important festival for Kashmiri Pandits, celebrated over 3 to 4 days with distinct local rituals.

major_festivals.name: Tulip Festival
major_festivals.significance: Spring festival held at the Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden in Srinagar during April bloom.

major_festivals.name: Hemis Festival
major_festivals.significance: Held at Hemis Gompa in Ladakh/J&K borders, famous for the sacred 'Cham' mask dance by Buddhist monks.

major_festivals.name: Sarhul
major_festivals.significance: Tribal New Year; Sal trees are worshiped as their flowers bloom, representing a bond with nature.

major_festivals.name: Karam Festival
major_festivals.significance: Worship of the Karam tree deity for power, wealth, and a bountiful harvest.

major_festivals.name: Tusu Parab
major_festivals.significance: Winter harvest festival celebrated on Makar Sankranti by young unmarried girls with songs.

major_festivals.name: Mysuru Dasara
major_festivals.significance: Grand 10-day celebration featuring the illuminated Mysore Palace and the Jumboo Savari (elephant procession).

major_festivals.name: Ugadi
major_festivals.significance: Kannada New Year celebrated with joy and family feasts across the state.

major_festivals.name: Kambala
major_festivals.significance: Traditional annual buffalo race held in muddy paddy fields of coastal Karnataka.

major_festivals.name: Hampi Utsav
major_festivals.significance: Mega cultural festival held amidst the ruins of the ancient Vijayanagara Empire.

major_festivals.name: Onam
major_festivals.significance: State festival of Kerala; commemorates King Mahabali's return; famous for Pookalam (floral carpets), Sadhya (feast), and Vallamkali (snake boat races).

major_festivals.name: Vishu
major_festivals.significance: Astronomical New Year; the first thing seen in the morning is the 'Vishwukkani' (auspicious arrangement) for good luck.

major_festivals.name: Thrissur Pooram
major_festivals.significance: Held at Vadakkunnathan Temple; magnificent display of caparisoned elephants, Kudamattom (umbrella exchange), and high-energy percussion (Panchavadyam).

major_festivals.name: Khajuraho Dance Festival
major_festivals.significance: A week-long festival highlighting India's top classical dancers against the backdrop of Khajuraho temples.

major_festivals.name: Tansen Music Festival
major_festivals.significance: Held annually in Gwalior near the tomb of legendary singer Tansen to honor Indian classical music masters.

major_festivals.name: Bhagoria Haat Festival
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated by Bhil and Bhilala tribes ahead of Holi; serves as a traditional match-making and agricultural fair.

major_festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
major_festivals.significance: Publicly popularized by Bal Gangadhar Tilak to unify people; features huge pandals and massive public immersion processions.

major_festivals.name: Gudi Padwa
major_festivals.significance: Marathi New Year, marked by hoisting a decorated 'Gudi' outside windows to signify victory and prosperity.

major_festivals.name: Banganga Festival
major_festivals.significance: Musical event held at the ancient Banganga Tank in Malabar Hill, Mumbai.

major_festivals.name: Yaoshang
major_festivals.significance: Manipur's version of Holi, lasting 5 days; famous for the 'Thabal Chongba' (moonlight dance).

major_festivals.name: Sangai Festival
major_festivals.significance: The state's grandest tourism festival, named after the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer).

major_festivals.name: Cheiraoba
major_festivals.significance: Manipur New Year; locals climb nearby hilltops as a ritual to symbolize rising to greater achievements.

major_festivals.name: Chumpha Festival
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated by the Tangkhul Naga tribe right after harvesting the crops.

major_festivals.name: Wangala Festival (100 Drums)
major_festivals.significance: Post-harvest thanksgiving festival of the Garo tribe; features rhythmic beating of 100 long drums simultaneously.

major_festivals.name: Nongkrem Dance Festival
major_festivals.significance: 5-day religious festival of the Khasi tribe for peace, a good harvest, and prosperity.

major_festivals.name: Cherry Blossom Festival
major_festivals.significance: Annual autumn festival in Shillong matching Japan's sakura blooms, complete with indie rock shows.

major_festivals.name: Chapchar Kut
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated upon the completion of the grueling clearing of bamboo forest for Jhum farming; features the famous Cheraw (bamboo) dance.

major_festivals.name: Mim Kut & Pawl Kut
major_festivals.significance: Festivals celebrated after maize and paddy harvests to thank ancestors and local spirits.

major_festivals.name: Hornbill Festival
major_festivals.significance: Known as the 'Festival of Festivals'; held from Dec 1-10 at Kisama Heritage Village to showcase the unity and dance forms of all 17 Naga tribes.

major_festivals.name: Moatsu Mong
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated by the Ao Naga tribe in May after completing the sowing of seeds, full of dynamic community singing.

major_festivals.name: Sekrenyi
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated by the Angami Naga tribe; focused on cleansing rituals to banish past sins and ensure warriors are purified.

major_festivals.name: Ratha Yatra
major_festivals.significance: The chariot festival of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra at Puri, attracting global crowds.

major_festivals.name: Nuakhai
major_festivals.significance: Agricultural festival of Western Odisha to welcome the new rice crop of the season.

major_festivals.name: Raja Parba
major_festivals.significance: A 3-day festival celebrating womanhood and the menstruation period of Mother Earth; no farm work is allowed.

major_festivals.name: Bali Jatra
major_festivals.significance: Held in Cuttack on Kartik Purnima to celebrate ancient maritime trade voyages to Bali, Sumatra, and Java.

major_festivals.name: Baisakhi
major_festivals.significance: Marks the harvest of Rabi crops and the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.

major_festivals.name: Lohri
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated in January with bonfires, rewari, and peanuts to mark the passing of the coldest winter days.

major_festivals.name: Hola Mohalla
major_festivals.significance: Gathering at Anandpur Sahib right after Holi, showcasing traditional Sikh martial arts (Gatka) and mock military battles.

major_festivals.name: Pushkar Camel Fair
major_festivals.significance: World's largest camel and livestock trading fair, combining colorful cultural competitions on the banks of Pushkar Lake.

major_festivals.name: Gangaur Festival
major_festivals.significance: Worship of Shiva (Isa) and Parvati (Gauri) by women for martial bliss and long life of spouses.

major_festivals.name: Desert Festival
major_festivals.significance: Held in Jaisalmer, featuring camel races, turban tying, and longest mustache competitions.

major_festivals.name: Saga Dawa
major_festivals.significance: Most sacred Buddhist festival, commemorating the birth, enlightenment, and parinirvana of Lord Buddha.

major_festivals.name: Losoong / Namsoong
major_festivals.significance: Bhutia and Lepcha New Year, celebrated at the end of the harvest season with Black Hat mask dances.

major_festivals.name: Pang Lhabsol
major_festivals.significance: Unique festival paying homage to Mount Khangchendzonga as the guardian deity of Sikkim.

major_festivals.name: Pongal
major_festivals.significance: 4-day harvest festival equivalent to Thanksgiving; features Bhogi, Thai Pongal (cooking sweet rice), Maattu Pongal (worshiping cattle), and Kaanum Pongal.

major_festivals.name: Puthandu
major_festivals.significance: Tamil New Year, celebrated on the first day of Chithirai month.

major_festivals.name: Jallikattu Utsav
major_festivals.significance: Bull-taming event conducted as part of Maattu Pongal celebrations.

major_festivals.name: Natyanjali Dance Festival
major_festivals.significance: Annual classical tribute to Lord Nataraja at the Chidambaram temple during Mahashivratri.

major_festivals.name: Bathukamma
major_festivals.significance: A gorgeous 9-day floral festival celebrated by women stack-building concentric layers of local seasonal flowers.

major_festivals.name: Bonalu
major_festivals.significance: Monsoon festival honoring Goddess Mahakali; women carry earthen pots cooked with rice, milk, and jaggery to offer the deity.

major_festivals.name: Sammakka Saralamma Jatara
major_festivals.significance: The world's largest tribal gathering, celebrating a mother-daughter fight against unjust taxes imposed by rulers.

major_festivals.name: Kharchi Puja
major_festivals.significance: Worship of the 14 structural deities of the royal family, involving cleansing rituals for the earth.

major_festivals.name: Garia Puja
major_festivals.significance: Celebrated to pray for a bounty crop, livestock health, and general safety from diseases.

major_festivals.name: Kumbh Mela
major_festivals.significance: Inscribed on UNESCO's intangible list; rotates across Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik every 12 years.

major_festivals.name: Lathmar Holi
major_festivals.significance: Unique Holi played in Barsana and Nandgaon where women playfully beat men with wooden sticks.

major_festivals.name: Taj Mahotsav
major_festivals.significance: 10-day spring carnival at Agra showcasing Mughal-era artisan traditions and classical ghazals.

major_festivals.name: Phool Dei
major_festivals.significance: Young girls place fresh spring flowers on the doorsteps of local houses to bring good fortune.

major_festivals.name: Ganga Dussehra
major_festivals.significance: Celebrates the historical descent of the holy river Ganga from heaven to Earth.

major_festivals.name: Durga Puja
major_festivals.significance: Inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list; transforms Kolkata into an open-air art gallery of magnificent themed pandals.

major_festivals.name: Poila Baisakh
major_festivals.significance: Bengali New Year, marked by opening new accounting ledgers (Haal Khata) and sweet distributions.

major_festivals.name: Gangasagar Mela
major_festivals.significance: Second-largest gathering in India after Kumbh, held on Makar Sankranti where the Hooghly river meets the Bay of Bengal.
